هُوتَةٌ (K) and ↓ هَوْتَةٌ (S, K) A low, or depressed, tract, or piece, of land: (S, K:) or a deep place: (IAth:) or the space between two mountains: (IAar:) pl. هُوَتٌ (as in the CK) or هُوت (as in the TA.) It may be said that هُوتٌ and هُوَتٌ are coll. gen. ns. [of each of which the n. un. is with ة]. (TA.) ―
-b2- Also هُوتَةٌ A road, or way, descending to water. (IAar.) ―
-b3- صَبَّ اللّٰهُ عَلَيْهِ وَمْوَتَةً ↓ هَوْتَةَ an imprecation, respecting which ISd says, I know not what is هوتة here. [It probably signifies A cry, such as destroyed the tribe of Thamood: see هَوَّتَ.] (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
